stem: Before a flag has been raised, inclement weather—a typhoon signal is raised in the locality—begins. A custodian proposes raising it anyway because daytime display is usual. Under RA 8491, Section 16, which assessment is correct?

Raise it because the rule for an already-raised flag governs every case
Raise it at half-mast because rain authorizes that position
Raise it with red uppermost because the weather changes orientation

explanation: Section 16 says not to raise the flag in inclement weather, but says that if already raised it shall not be lowered. The initial status matters; half-mast and red-field display have separate bases. Section 3(h) supplies the local typhoon-signal meaning of inclement weather.

Keep it at the peak until closing, then pause at half-mast

stem: For an authorized flag-draped casket, a plan places the white triangle at the head but puts blue over its left side and proposes lowering the flag into the grave. Which repair satisfies both relevant Section 24 requirements?

Keep blue over the left side; remove/fold the flag and hand it to heirs before interment
Put blue over the right side; retain the flag into the grave
Keep blue over the left side; retain the flag into the grave

explanation: The triangle at the head is already correct. Section 24 requires blue over the casket’s right side and forbids lowering the flag into the grave; solemn folding and handover to heirs complete the stated handling.

Keep first-note timing; raise slowly with blue uppermost
Keep first-note timing; raise briskly with red uppermost
Wait until the last note; raise briskly with blue uppermost

explanation: First-note timing is already correct. Section 21 requires brisk ascent and Section 10 requires blue uppermost in peace. Changing only speed or orientation leaves a defect; delaying to the last note breaks timing.

Change to brisk descent, finish at the last note, then fold solemnly
Keep slow descent, finish at the last note, then leave it unfolded

At closing raise briefly to the peak, then lower briskly at the first note

stem: A household appliance is sold with the full price due next month in one payment. Which reading of RA 7394’s consumer-credit definition is accurate?

choices.text: Future full payment can qualify even without installments
Only multiple installments can qualify
Future payment cannot qualify without a credit card
The definition applies only after a missed deadline

explanation: Article 4(o) expressly permits future payment in full or installments. Cards and delinquency are not required elements.

stem: A supplier solicits a natural person to buy household goods, but no sale occurs. For RA 7394, Article 4(s), which conclusion about consumer transactions is supported?

choices.text: Solicitation/promotion of a covered transaction is included
Only completed delivery is included
Only installment repayment is included
Only a completed insurance contract is included

explanation: The definition includes supplier solicitation/promotion concerning covered transactions. Completion is not essential; the text separately excludes specified securities/insurance dispositions.

stem: Apply only RA 7394’s definitions. Plan A sells goods but derives profits primarily from investment-linked recruitment, with a fixed membership cap. Product B is correctly attributed to its real manufacturer but is expensive. Which assessment is supported?

choices.text: A can meet the pyramid definition despite goods/cap; B is not shown counterfeit by price alone
A cannot be a pyramid because goods exist; B is not shown counterfeit by price alone
A can meet the pyramid definition; B is necessarily counterfeit because costly
A cannot be a pyramid because capped; B is necessarily counterfeit because costly

explanation: Article 4(k) addresses primarily recruitment profits and rejects a cap exception; 4(v) requires false unauthorized attribution, not a high price. Each rival preserves one conclusion but corrupts the other.

stem: Two draft consumer policies are reviewed under RA 7394, Article 2. Policy P funds clear product information but excludes consumer representatives from social/economic policy formulation. Policy Q provides representative participation but removes means of redress because prevention is preferred. Which revision addresses both omissions?

choices.text: P: preserve information and add representative involvement; Q: preserve participation and restore redress
P: preserve information and add representative involvement; Q: preserve participation but retain removal of redress
P: preserve information but retain exclusion of representatives; Q: preserve participation and restore redress
P: preserve information but retain exclusion of representatives; Q: preserve participation and retain removal of redress

explanation: Article 2 includes information/education, redress and consumer-representative involvement together. Each policy’s existing strength should remain while its missing objective is restored; one objective does not substitute for another.
